author: rule-family designer (world: 4-7 letter common English words; lineup answer)
description: WORD RULE-FAMILY class, REVISION 2 = LINEUP ANSWER (docs/RULE_FAMILIES.md sec. "Revision 2", 2026-09-05; brainstorm and full tables in challenges/lab/NOTES_rules_words.md; v1 kept as challenges/lab/tavrik.v1.json). World = 4-7 letter common English words. CLUE = 2 or 3 example words, one per line, lowercase (56 % two, 44 % three); then a BLANK LINE; then FOUR candidate words, one per line, all real words drawn from the same 4501-word pool as the examples and all of the SAME length as each other. ANSWER = the one candidate that obeys the hidden rule, written back verbatim (case- and whitespace-insensitive) or as its 1-based index 1..4. Exactly one candidate obeys the rule (verified in generate on every clue), so the floor is 1/4 = 25 %. v1's "the answer must be >= 2 edits from every clue word" clause is GONE (revision 2 sec.5): with a lineup there is nothing to be well formed about, and that clause was the single thing worth most to the round-1 winner (0/4 -> 29/38 once they guessed it). WHY THE LINEUP: in the first arena the two Opus teams scored 71 % and 66 % on v1 with NO demo and without ever naming a rule -- they kept every predicate of a ~273-strong word-predicate pool that was true of all the examples and emitted a word satisfying all of them at once; the true rule is in the pool, so the answer satisfied it by construction. A choice cannot be constructed: the player must say WHICH word is right, and the decoys are built so that every generic statistic points nowhere. UNIVERSE U: unchanged from v1 -- 10 templates, 25 one-breath rules, an ANTICHAIN verified by brute force over the 4501-word pool AND over all 56176 dictionary words of length 4-7 (positive examples can never separate a rule from a looser rule containing it, which is why the contains-c and ends-with-c grids are letter-disjoint and the ends-with grid holds no vowels). (0) the word has exactly n vowels, n in 1,3,4 [density .220 .220 .020]; (1) it has a double letter [.158]; (2) it starts and ends with the same letter [.046]; (3) it starts with a vowel [.132]; (4) its letters are in alphabetical order [.016]; (5) it has a c in it, c in b f k m p v w [.070-.149]; (6) it ends with c, c in d g l n r s t y [.046-.114]; (7) it has a j, q, x or z in it [.048]; (8) it uses only three different letters [.047]; (9) some letter turns up three times [.023]. ELIGIBILITY (new): template 0, "exactly n vowels", is now a COMPETITOR ONLY -- it stays in U and the examples must still kill it, but it is never the hidden rule, because its two loose cousins ("at least as many vowels as the least vowelly example" and "at most as many as the most vowelly one") bracket it EXACTLY, so on such a clue no decoy could ever fire the same excluded rules as the truth and revision 2 sec.5b would be impossible. The other 9 templates / 22 rules are drawn uniformly by template first and then parameter (mix over 2000 clues 201-247 per template, expected 222); mean density of the hidden rule 0.073. THE LINEUP. generate draws the rule, then a MINIMAL identifying example set (all of them together leave exactly one rule of U alive, no proper subset does; uniqueness 500/500, minimality 500/500), and then builds four candidates of one length in which every decoy is made to look like the truth in three ways. (a) TRAP PROFILE, revision 2 sec.5b: all four candidates fire EXACTLY the same set of example-consistent excluded rules (500/500), so no trap -- and no count of traps -- separates them and every trap heuristic scores exactly 25.0 %. (b) SHAPE: the decoys use the same number of different letters as the true candidate wherever the rule allows it; without this, "pick the odd one out by shared letters" scored 46 % (73-74 % on the three-different-letters and letter-three-times clues, whose answers are naturally the letter-poorest word of the four) and now scores 24.3 %. (c) THE ATTACKER'S OWN COUNT: generate carries dornic1b's tavrik_preds() -- all 273 predicates, rebuilt bit for bit, duplicate keys and their shadowing included -- intersects it over the examples and aims the true candidate's RANK on that count, so that at least one decoy out-counts the truth on 52.6 % of clues (revision 2 sec.2 asks for >= 40 %) and among the four the truth is the sole top scorer only 47 % of the time. Result: "pick the candidate satisfying the most surviving pool predicates" scores 34.0 %, its inverse 26.9 %. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED RULES (never in U; the decoys' sponsors; "fits" = the rule fitted to the clue is consistent with every example, so a player who forms it is never contradicted): at least as many vowels as the least vowelly example 100 %; at most as many vowels as the most vowelly example 100 %; it ends with a consonant 68 %; it contains every letter the examples share 63 %; it starts with a consonant 49 %; more consonants than vowels 49 %; the second letter is a vowel 29 %; the same number of letters as the examples 24 %; the second letter is a consonant 17 %; no letter is repeated 9 %; two vowels side by side 4 %; it rhymes, same last two letters 4 %; the same first letter as the examples 2 %; it ends with a vowel 1 %. Mean 5.2 of them are consistent with any one clue (min 2, max 9) and every decoy fires at least one (500/500) -- but because the true candidate fires exactly the same ones, EVERY one of those rows scores exactly 25.0 %. Also excluded by construction: any rule about LENGTH (all four candidates are the same length, so it cannot help), about the MIDDLE of the word, about SOUND or MEANING, about the common letters (only b f k m p v w are ever asked for, so "they all have an e" is never the answer), and any LOOSE statement -- this class only ever says "exactly", "is", "there is a". Knowing what it never says is now worth nothing on its own; only knowing what it DOES say pays. WITNESSES over 500 fresh clues (seeds 1e6..1e6+499): the in-U intersection, i.e. a player who knows U, 100.0 %; the true rule (solve) 100.0 %, and 100.0 % answering by index; the candidate satisfying the MOST example-consistent predicates of the 273-strong outside pool 34.0 %; the smallest edit distance to an example 28.7 %; the most vowels 28.3 %; the most letters in place with an example 27.9 %; alphabetically first 27.6 %; pick candidate 1 27.0 %; the FEWEST pool predicates 26.9 %; a random candidate 25.0 %; the outlier of the four by shared letters 24.3 %; shares the most letters with an example 23.0 %; the most different letters 22.6 %; the medoid of the four 21.0 %; each of the 14 excluded rules exactly 25.0 %; a player whose universe is U plus those 14, committing to a random survivor, 38.6 %; a player who knows U minus its two rarest templates (alphabetical order .016 and some letter three times .023) 83.7 % -- 81-85 % for any other pair, since a subset universe leaves them zero survivors on the clues they cannot see, so they know they are lost and guess. True-candidate position over 500 clues 135/113/122/130; rank by pool-predicate count 237/86/98/79; candidate length 4/5/6/7 = 92/141/154/113. SOLVE re-derives the survivor exactly as the scorer does and returns the candidate that obeys it (there is nothing left to vary: the answer is a choice). SCORE is 689 chars (v1: 821; still needs max_score_code_chars = 1024, the raise RULE_FAMILIES.md sec.4 allows for this paradigm): it splits the clue on the blank line, resolves an ASCII index or a verbatim candidate, rebuilds all 25 rules of U, filters them by the examples, insists on a single survivor and checks that the CHOSEN CANDIDATE obeys it -- a word that is not in the lineup scores 0, which is what kills the construction attack, and words.is_word is no longer needed at all. No hidden channel. DEMOS: "tissue/capped" + [reader decree madame decade] -> decree (it has a double letter); "kick/food" + [rural dummy rebel level] -> level (it uses only three different letters); "squeeze/execute/express" + [yours human today major] -> major (it has a j, q, x or z in it). PREDICTED: 25-40 % without a demo (the shape reads as multiple choice, so every probe is well formed and the floor is free; the round-1 method degrades to counting predicates, 34 %), 40-70 % with one (a demo teaches the format in one look; from there every cheap statistic is worth 25 % and the only way up is reconstructing U -- a player who has mapped 7 of the 9 eligible templates scores 84 %, one who has all 9 scores 100 %). Mean across two Opus teams ~ 0.35-0.55, i.e. classification calibrated, with the risk now on the HARD side rather than the easy one: v1's 6 % -> 21 % -> 100 % ladder is replaced by 25 % -> 34 % -> 100 %.

VOW = "aeiou"

# --- the universe U: 10 templates, 25 one-breath rules (unchanged from v1) ----
U = [(0, "1"), (0, "3"), (0, "4"),      # the word has exactly n vowels
     (1, ""),                            # it has a double letter
     (2, ""),                            # it starts and ends with the same letter
     (3, ""),                            # it starts with a vowel
     (4, ""),                            # its letters are in alphabetical order
     (7, ""),                            # it has a j, q, x or z in it
     (8, ""),                            # it uses only three different letters
     (9, "")] + \
    [(5, c) for c in "bfkmpvw"] + \
    [(6, c) for c in "dglnrsty"]         # ... a letter three times / contains c / ends with c


def P(r, w):
    """Is word w an instance of rule r? (every parameter is a string so the list is safe)"""
    t, q = r
    return [str(sum(c in VOW for c in w)) == q,
            any(w[i] == w[i + 1] for i in range(len(w) - 1)),
            w[0] == w[-1],
            w[0] in VOW,
            list(w) == sorted(w),
            q in w,
            w[-1] == q,
            any(c in "jqxz" for c in w),
            len(set(w)) == 3,
            max(w.count(c) for c in w) > 2][t]


def near(x, y):
    """True if x is y, or one letter changed / added / removed. Used only to keep the
    EXAMPLES apart -- there is no freshness clause on the answer any more."""
    if len(x) == len(y):
        return sum(p != q for p, q in zip(x, y)) < 2
    if len(x) > len(y):
        x, y = y, x
    return len(y) - len(x) == 1 and any(y[:i] + y[i + 1:] == x for i in range(len(y)))


# --- what the EXCLUDED (trap) rules read off a word --------------------------
def XFEAT(w):
    """(letter set, #vowels, length, first letter, last two letters, a letter repeats,
        2nd letter is a vowel, two vowels side by side, last letter is a vowel,
        more consonants than vowels)"""
    ls = 0
    for c in w:
        ls |= 1 << (ord(c) - 97)
    nv = 0
    for c in w:
        if c in VOW:
            nv += 1
    return (ls, nv, len(w), w[0], w[-2:], len(set(w)) < len(w), w[1] in VOW,
            any(w[i] in VOW and w[i + 1] in VOW for i in range(len(w) - 1)),
            w[-1] in VOW, (len(w) - nv) * 2 > len(w))


def TRAPS(X):
    """The excluded rules -- never in U -- that are consistent with EVERY example
    (X = the examples' XFEATs). Each is a (code, parameter) pair read by TBITS."""
    t = []
    sh = X[0][0]
    for x in X:
        sh &= x[0]
    if sh:
        t.append((0, sh))                                  # has every letter they share
    t.append((1, min(x[1] for x in X)))                    # >= the least vowelly example
    t.append((2, max(x[1] for x in X)))                    # <= the most vowelly example
    if all(x[9] for x in X):
        t.append((3, 0))                                   # more consonants than vowels
    if all(x[3] not in VOW for x in X):
        t.append((4, 0))                                   # it starts with a consonant
    if all(x[6] for x in X):
        t.append((5, 0))                                   # the 2nd letter is a vowel
    if not any(x[6] for x in X):
        t.append((6, 0))                                   # the 2nd letter is a consonant
    if len(set(x[2] for x in X)) == 1:
        t.append((7, X[0][2]))                             # the same number of letters
    if not any(x[5] for x in X):
        t.append((8, 0))                                   # no letter is repeated
    if len(set(x[3] for x in X)) == 1:
        t.append((9, X[0][3]))                             # the same first letter
    if len(set(x[4] for x in X)) == 1:
        t.append((10, X[0][4]))                            # it rhymes (same last two)
    if all(x[7] for x in X):
        t.append((11, 0))                                  # two vowels side by side
    if all(x[8] for x in X):
        t.append((12, 0))                                  # it ends with a vowel
    if not any(x[8] for x in X):
        t.append((13, 0))                                  # it ends with a consonant
    return t


def TBITS(t, x):
    m = 0
    for k, c in enumerate(t):
        h = c[0]
        if h == 0:
            b = x[0] & c[1] == c[1]
        elif h == 1:
            b = x[1] >= c[1]
        elif h == 2:
            b = x[1] <= c[1]
        elif h == 3:
            b = x[9]
        elif h == 4:
            b = x[3] not in VOW
        elif h == 5:
            b = x[6]
        elif h == 6:
            b = not x[6]
        elif h == 7:
            b = x[2] == c[1]
        elif h == 8:
            b = not x[5]
        elif h == 9:
            b = x[3] == c[1]
        elif h == 10:
            b = x[4] == c[1]
        elif h == 11:
            b = x[7]
        elif h == 12:
            b = x[8]
        else:
            b = not x[8]
        if b:
            m |= 1 << k
    return m


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The OUTSIDE predicate pool: the 279 word predicates the round-1 winner
# (dornic1b) actually brought to this class, rebuilt bit for bit -- lengths,
# per-letter has/starts/ends/doubles/twice/thrice, vowel and consonant counts,
# distinct-letter counts, repeat profiles, vowel-shape, affixes, syllables.
# The lineup is balanced against it: the true candidate must not stand out as
# the one satisfying the most example-consistent predicates, which is exactly
# how v1 was cracked (66 % with no demo, by intersection).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
AZ = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
SUF = ("ing", "ed", "er", "ly", "s", "y", "e", "ion", "al", "ful", "ss", "ll", "tt", "pp")
PRE = ("un", "re", "in", "ex", "de", "pro", "con", "a", "o", "i", "e", "u", "b", "c")


def SYL(w):
    n = 0
    prev = False
    for c in w:
        v = c in VOW
        if v and not prev:
            n += 1
        prev = v
    if w.endswith("e") and n > 1:
        n -= 1
    return n


def PRED(w):
    L = len(w)
    cnt = {}
    for c in w:
        cnt[c] = cnt.get(c, 0) + 1
    nd = len(cnt)
    nv = 0
    for c in w:
        if c in VOW:
            nv += 1
    nc = L - nv
    mx = max(cnt.values())
    nrep = sum(1 for v in cnt.values() if v >= 2)
    v = [L == k for k in range(3, 10)]
    v += [L % 2 == 0, L % 2 == 1]
    for ch in AZ:                      # 'stv/stc/env/enc/dblv/dblc' are shadowed below,
        k = cnt.get(ch, 0)             # exactly as they are in the player's own dict
        v += [k > 0, k == 2, k >= 3]
        if ch not in "cv":
            v += [w[0] == ch, w[-1] == ch, ch + ch in w]
    dbl = any(w[i] == w[i + 1] for i in range(L - 1))
    v += [dbl, not dbl, w[0] == w[-1], w == w[::-1]]
    for k in range(1, 9):
        v += [nd == k, nv == k, nc == k, mx >= k, mx == k, nrep == k]
    v += [nd == L, nd < L]
    v += [w[0] in VOW, w[-1] in VOW, w[0] not in VOW, w[-1] not in VOW,
          w[1] in VOW, w[1] not in VOW,
          w[-1] not in VOW and w[-2] not in VOW, w[-1] in VOW and w[-2] in VOW,
          w[0] not in VOW and w[1] not in VOW, w[0] in VOW and w[1] in VOW]
    a2 = any(w[i] in VOW and w[i + 1] in VOW for i in range(L - 1))
    c3 = any(all(w[i + j] not in VOW for j in range(3)) for i in range(L - 2))
    v += [a2, not a2,
          all((w[i] in VOW) != (w[i + 1] in VOW) for i in range(L - 1)),
          c3, not c3, list(w) == sorted(w)]
    v += [w.endswith(s) for s in SUF]
    v += [w.startswith(s) for s in PRE]
    v += [any(w[i] == w[i + 1] and w[i] in VOW for i in range(L - 1)),
          any(w[i] == w[i + 1] and w[i] not in VOW for i in range(L - 1)),
          w[0] == w[-1], (w[0] in VOW) == (w[-1] in VOW), nv * 2 == L, nc * 2 > L,
          any(c in "jqxzkvwy" for c in w), not any(c in "jqxz" for c in w),
          any(abs(ord(w[i]) - ord(w[i + 1])) == 1 for i in range(L - 1)),
          w[0] == w[1], w[0] in w[1:]]
    s = SYL(w)
    v += [s == k for k in range(1, 6)]
    return v


# ---- tables built once per worker (not charged to max_generate_ms) ----------
BIT = {}
for _k, _r in enumerate(U):
    BIT[_r] = 1 << _k
MASK = []
XF = []
ND = []
PMS = []
BYLEN = {}
for _i, _w in enumerate(POOL):
    _m = 0
    for _r in U:
        if P(_r, _w):
            _m |= BIT[_r]
    MASK.append(_m)
    XF.append(XFEAT(_w))
    ND.append(len(set(_w)))
    _p = 0
    for _j, _b in enumerate(PRED(_w)):
        if _b:
            _p |= 1 << _j
    PMS.append(_p)
    BYLEN.setdefault(len(_w), []).append(_i)
SAT = [[i for i, m in enumerate(MASK) if m >> j & 1] for j in range(len(U))]
SATL = []
for j in range(len(U)):
    d = {}
    for i in SAT[j]:
        d.setdefault(len(POOL[i]), []).append(i)
    SATL.append(d)
# ELIG: the templates that may be the HIDDEN rule. "exactly n vowels" (template 0) stays in
# U as a COMPETITOR the examples must kill, but is never the answer: its two loose cousins,
# "at least as many vowels as the least vowelly example" and "at most as many as the most
# vowelly one", bracket it EXACTLY, so no decoy can ever fire the same traps as the truth.
ELIG = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9]
BYT = {t: [j for j, r in enumerate(U) if r[0] == t] for t in ELIG}


def BUILD(r, g, CN, t, rho):
    """Assemble the four lines. `rho` of the decoys beat the true candidate on the outside
    predicate count and the other 3 - rho do not; among the triples that respect that split
    we take one that puts the truth at a randomly aimed place in the mutual letter-overlap
    order too, so "pick the odd one out" is worth nothing either."""
    c = CN[t]
    hi = [i for i in g if CN[i] > c]
    lo = [i for i in g if CN[i] <= c]
    tm = XF[t][0]
    aim = r.randrange(4)
    best = None
    bd = 9
    for _q in range(12):
        r.shuffle(hi)
        r.shuffle(lo)
        sel = hi[:rho] + lo[:3 - rho]
        ms = [XF[i][0] for i in sel] + [tm]
        ov = []
        for a in range(4):
            v = 0
            for b in range(4):
                if a != b:
                    v += (ms[a] & ms[b]).bit_count()
            ov.append(v)
        dd = abs(sum(1 for v in ov[:3] if v < ov[3]) - aim)
        if dd < bd:
            bd = dd
            best = sel
            if dd == 0:
                break
    out = [POOL[i] for i in best] + [POOL[t]]
    r.shuffle(out)
    return out


def LINEUP(r, j, ex, C, tr):
    """Four real words of ONE length, exactly one of which obeys the rule.

    Every decoy breaks the rule but is built to look like the true candidate in three ways:
    it fires EXACTLY the same excluded rules (so no trap - and no count of traps - tells them
    apart); it uses the same number of different letters, where the rule allows that (without
    it, "pick the odd one out" cracked the double-letter and three-different-letters clues);
    and the four counts of example-consistent OUTSIDE predicates bracket the true candidate's,
    so the version-space attack that cracked v1 - "answer with the thing that satisfies every
    predicate the clue still allows" - has nothing to grip."""
    b = 1 << j
    d = SATL[j]
    ES = set(ex)
    LS = [L for L in d if len(d[L]) > 3 and len(BYLEN[L]) > 200]
    r.shuffle(LS)
    want = r.randrange(4)
    back = None
    bq = 99
    for L in LS:
        pool = BYLEN[L]
        n = len(pool)
        sat = d[L]
        DG = {}
        SG = {}
        seen = set()
        for _s in range(260):              # decoys: same length, rule broken, a trap fired
            i = pool[r.randrange(n)]
            if i in seen or MASK[i] & b or i in ES:
                continue
            seen.add(i)
            x = TBITS(tr, XF[i])
            if x:
                DG.setdefault((x, ND[i]), []).append(i)
        for i in (sat if len(sat) < 100 else r.sample(sat, 100)):   # the true candidate
            if i not in ES:
                SG.setdefault(TBITS(tr, XF[i]), []).append(i)
        CN = {}
        for x in SG:
            for i in SG[x]:
                # the weakest true candidates first: they are the ones a decoy can out-count
                CN[i] = (PMS[i] & C).bit_count()
            SG[x].sort(key=lambda i: CN[i])
            for i in SG[x]:
                for off in (0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3):
                    g = DG.get((x, ND[i] + off))
                    if g is None or len(g) < 3:
                        continue
                    for q in g:
                        if q not in CN:
                            CN[q] = (PMS[q] & C).bit_count()
                    hi = sum(1 for q in g if CN[q] > CN[i])
                    k = min(hi, want)
                    if k < 3 - len(g) + hi:
                        k = 3 - len(g) + hi
                    if k < 0 or k > hi:
                        break
                    qq = abs(off) * 4 + abs(k - want)
                    if qq < bq:
                        bq = qq
                        back = (g, CN, i, k)
                        if qq == 0:
                            return BUILD(r, g, CN, i, k)
                    break
    if back:
        return BUILD(r, back[0], back[1], back[2], back[3])
    return None


def EXAMPLES(r, j, cand, A):
    """A MINIMAL identifying set: all of them together leave exactly one rule of U alive
    while no proper subset does. A triple first, else a pair."""
    best = None
    for _t in range(30):                    # a MINIMAL identifying triple
        T = r.sample(cand, 3)
        m = MASK[T[0]] & MASK[T[1]]
        if m.bit_count() < 2:
            continue
        if (MASK[T[0]] & MASK[T[2]]).bit_count() < 2:
            continue
        if (MASK[T[1]] & MASK[T[2]]).bit_count() < 2:
            continue
        if (m & MASK[T[2]]).bit_count() != 1:
            continue
        ws = [POOL[i] for i in T]
        if near(ws[0], ws[1]) or near(ws[0], ws[2]) or near(ws[1], ws[2]):
            continue
        best = T
        break
    if best is None:                        # ... else a minimal pair
        for _t in range(30):
            T = r.sample(A, 2)
            if MASK[T[0]].bit_count() < 2 or MASK[T[1]].bit_count() < 2:
                continue
            if (MASK[T[0]] & MASK[T[1]]).bit_count() != 1:
                continue
            if near(POOL[T[0]], POOL[T[1]]):
                continue
            best = T
            break
    return best


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    for _ in range(120):
        j = r.choice(BYT[r.choice(ELIG)])       # template first, then parameter
        A = SAT[j]
        if len(A) < 12:
            continue
        Ar = [i for i in A if MASK[i].bit_count() > 3]   # words that satisfy many rules of U
        for _e in range(4):                     # up to four minimal example sets per rule --
            cand = Ar if (len(Ar) > 11 and r.random() < .5) else A   # a "contains c" clue
            best = EXAMPLES(r, j, cand, A)      # whose words share only c cannot be balanced
            if best is None:
                break
            C = -1                              # the outside predicates the examples allow
            for i in best:
                C &= PMS[i]
            tr = TRAPS([XF[i] for i in best])
            line = LINEUP(r, j, best, C, tr)
            if line is not None:
                return "\n".join(POOL[i] for i in best) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(line)
    # never reached in 20000 seeds, but kept scoreable all the same: the single
    # survivor of these two examples is "it has a double letter"
    return "kitty\nsoccer\n\nlesson\nmarket\ncousin\nrandom"

def p(r, w):

    return [str(sum(c in "aeiou" for c in w)) == q,
            any(w[i] == w[i + 1] for i in range(len(w) - 1)),
            w[0] == w[-1], w[0] in "aeiou", list(w) == sorted(w), q in w, w[-1] == q,
            any(c in "jqxz" for c in w), len(set(w)) == 3,

def solve(clue):
    B = clue.strip().split("\n\n")
    E = B[0].split("\n")
    K = B[1].split("\n")
    V = [r for r in U if all(p(r, e) for e in E)]   # the same enumeration the scorer does
